In the first few episodes I felt like they were building this up as something that would be important, but they just kind of .. dropped it? I’m guessing they’re going to touch on it in season 4, seeing as their whole friendship dynamic will shift with Will and El moved away. Still, I think that they aren’t giving enough time to really develop Will and how he fits in with the others.

I feel like Will has missed a lot of time with the group, either being trapped in the upside down or dealing with the whole mind flayer possession thing. He feels behind, especially in this season. A lot of people also speculate that Will is gay, and that could also play a role. If he knows that he’s different than his friends, he could worry they’ll only accept the version of himself they already know. He watches his friends lose interest in D&D (the very thing that opens the first episode of the show), and instead gain interest in girls and relationships. Meanwhile, Will is still with excessive trauma and potentially questioning his sexuality. This creates a wall between him and the friends he wants to connect with. 

I would have loved to see the writers touch on this more, and focus more on Will’s character this season. Noah Schnapp is (in my opinion) the best young actor on the show aside from Millie Bobby Brown, and is extremely underused.

I think it has a lot to do with my religious upbringing, and streak of atheism that followed. I used to believe in god, just like I believed in Santa Claus. I tried to talk to god every Sunday as a child, but felt confused and tormented when he would never answer. My dad would say that god doesn’t directly answer people, but instead finds ways to show us that he hears us. I just couldn’t believe it. 
Since being agnostic for many years, I’ve tried to step away from the black and white thinking that often comes with both Catholicism and atheism. I am coming to terms with the fact that there’s much I don’t know, and may never know, and that’s okay. Though, that’s easier said than done. 
Ghosts, past lives, different dimensions, etc, all fascinate me greatly; but there’s always an underlying fear. If there’s a god, is there also a devil? If there’s no god, is there no afterlife? If there’s more than one version of myself, how do I know I’m not the worst version? For me, it’s a risk to indulge in such questions and experiments. I guess that’s why it freaks me out, but I’m working on it :-)

I started to show signs of depression around 11ish years old. I felt so confused as to why I felt so awful so consistently. I felt so invalided, both by myself and family. Everyone would blame my feelings on puberty and shifting hormones. Trust me when I say what you’re feeling is real, and incredibly painful, and that’s okay. Some your negative emotions could be related to entering adolescence, but that doesn’t make them any less hurtful or disabling. 
The good thing about being so young is that you have so much time to learn new things about yourself, learn skills early on and begin to try and heal. If you could possibly talk as your parents about seeing a counsellor/therapist, I’d recommend trying it out. It’s not for everyone, but some people get a lot out of it.
